Spec inconsistency, for the lead. Refresh test 4 says that after incorrect_client_credentials 'the next read throws GITHUB_SIGN_IN_REQUIRED with no request'. That contradicts the frozen contract 3.4 ('Signed out or not configured: calls request(undefined) exactly once'), the first line of 6.4 and L-10. After an app clear, the store has no account (A2 projects as signed-out). I followed the contract:
- a read that starts after the clear is a signed-out read: one request(undefined), no Authorization, no token request;
- a call that had already seen the account (one joined to the refresh) gets GITHUB_SIGN_IN_REQUIRED with no request (L-14).
The test asserts both. If 'refuse until the user acts' is wanted, 3.4 and 6.4 need changing.

Spec gap: 3.7 and 6.8 say send() after close() is 'refused without a request' but name no code. I throw GITHUB_RENEWAL_UNAVAILABLE in every state, because it does not claim the account ended. U6's reason scan will see it as a literal.

Spec gap: 6.2 sketches `transient = 0` only on authorization_pending, while L-9 says 'at most 3 consecutive transient polls'. I reset the count on any non-transient answer (pending, slow_down, rate-limited), which is the L-9 reading.
Spec gap: 6.2's slow_down 'bodyInterval when valid' does not define 'valid'. I used step 1's rule (5.5): an integer from 1 to 300.

Interpretation: 6.8's table says close() waits only for a refresh in flight. L-8 says 'GitHub work'. close() also waits for a commit point being stored, within the same quitWaitMs. F5 is aborted, not waited for.

Interpretation: 6.4's usable() step 4 has no budget check. I added `!budget.refreshed`, so a call never starts a second refresh (L-14). A call whose budget is spent and whose token has expired gets GITHUB_RENEWAL_UNAVAILABLE, never a clear.

Naming note for the guard table: the table maps 'shape check' to 'device 8'. In my file, the malformed and unusable poll answers are device '4b', and device 8 is the success case. So G14 turned 4b red and left 8 green.

The file was moved out of the tree for red run 1 and replaced by a throwing stub for red run 2, so every committed test was seen red without the service. But the authoring order was not test-first, and I say so. Cause: I designed the service while reading spec 6. Fix: the red runs came after, with the service absent, and were redone on the final test files. Verified: red2 JSON, 54/54 and 66/66 red; service sha256 identical before and after.

Mistake: refresh tests 4 (the clearing codes) and 8 (persist failure) checked account.json and the vault index as soon as the read rejected. Where: tests/github-signin-refresh.test.ts, cases 4 and 8. Impact: 9 tests red on correct code; nothing delivered was affected. Cause: a waiter leaves on accountChanged during the clear's synchronous prologue (spec 6.4); the clear's locked part writes the disk afterwards. Fix: the tests now wait for the clear to reach disk (reachesDisk / until). Verified: 66/66, repeated runs.

Mistake: the second half of refresh 12 ('sign-out prologue is synchronous') started signOut() in a hook without awaiting it. Where: refresh case 12. Impact: teardown deleted the directory while the clear was still writing (ENOTEMPTY), red; nothing else affected. Cause: a fire-and-forget call. Fix: the promise is kept and awaited, and its status is asserted. Verified: 66/66.

Mistake: refresh case 3 could not catch 'the live pointer set before commit', and the refused-token case of 10 could not catch 'counted once per hold'. Where: refresh cases 3 and 10. Impact: two named guards would have had no red test. Cause: case 3 had one read, which waits on the refresh anyway, and case 10 used an 'at most 3' bound. Fix: case 3 adds a read that starts during the commit; case 10 asserts exactly 3 refreshes and a clear at least 60 s after the start. Verified: G03 and G28 red, controls green.

Mistake: under its mutation, the C-6 budget case went red only by the 15 s timeout. Where: refresh case 10, 'at most one refresh and one retry'. Impact: a weaker proof. Cause: the fake answered every refresh, so the mutated loop never ended. Fix: one queued answer. Verified: G09 re-run, red on an assertion.

Cause: a one-shot flag armed too early. Fix: it is armed just before the second read. Verified: 66/66.

Inherited (the previous builder's, fixed by me): WIP test 9b read the vault's index.json with readFileSync before the vault had ever persisted. That file does not exist until the first vault write, so the test would throw ENOENT on correct code. Fixed with an indexBytes() helper that returns null when absent, plus a check that no .bin file exists.

tests/github-signin-refresh.test.ts is new: refresh list 1-19, 66 tests, plus a 3.4 pass-through case. Where the spec had no injectable seam:
- Refresh 11's Stop case uses U3's real GitHubReader and asserts RUN_CANCELLED.
- The deadline case runs at the send() level, with AbortSignal.timeout(100), and asserts a TimeoutError that the reader maps to GITHUB_TIMEOUT. The reader's 20 s deadline is fixed in U3, so a real-reader deadline test would exceed vitest's 15 s timeout.

src/main/github-signin.ts exports exactly spec 3.7's surface: GitHubLimits, GITHUB_LIMITS, GitHubSignInDeps and GitHubSignIn with status, start, cancel, signOut, openTarget, send and close.
- Every error the service originates is a bare `new Error(code)` with no cause. The literal GITHUB_ codes are GITHUB_SIGN_IN_REQUIRED, GITHUB_RENEWAL_UNAVAILABLE and GITHUB_RATE_LIMIT, ready for U6's reason scan.
- Hold reasons are thrown as `new Error(hold.reason)`, typed CredentialError.
- The bridge codes NOT_IMPLEMENTED, ENCRYPTION_UNAVAILABLE and NOT_FOUND come only from start and openTarget.

Grants: each grant's expiry is Date.now() + grantMs (never the injected clock), with contexts github:read:, github:refresh: and github:user:<uuid>, revoked in finally. Tests run on an injected clock in 2031, so any use of now() would be refused (G40).
The ARCHITECTURE.md U5 sentence is one physical line, after U2's line, per the 'one physical line per unit' convention in the spec's As built section.
